requirements.requirement: Successive producers can submit newline-delimited job IDs through jobs.fifo without restarting the consumer.
requirements.summary: Two pre-reboot producer sessions and two post-reboot sessions appended valid jobs while the consumer PID remained unchanged within each sequence and the service stayed active.

requirements.requirement: Record every complete non-empty line in received.txt, ignore empty and incomplete lines, and retain prior records.
requirements.summary: The seeded previous-job remained first. Complete test lines were appended, while empty lines and the unterminated producer-one-incomplete fragment were absent from the final seven-line file.

requirements.requirement: Avoid a busy loop while no producer is connected.
requirements.summary: With no producer connected, the consumer was blocked in wait_for_partner and accumulated zero CPU ticks during the three-second sample; the final observation showed the same blocked state and zero CPU time.
Stopping the service terminated the old PID, produced a successful systemd deactivation with no traceback or exception, and allowed a clean subsequent start.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The repaired script compiled successfully with the installed Python 3.12 interpreter. Before and after observations consistently show RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: node1 had a healthy pre-restart service and retained data, an acknowledged reboot, a changed boot identity independently confirmed by lifecycle snapshots, recovered system/service/data state, and successful post-reboot producer processing.
limitations: The idle-CPU check was a bounded three-second sample, and line processing was tested with representative rather than exhaustive producer/write patterns.
Minor temporary staging and bytecode artifacts were left under /tmp; this affects hygiene but not demonstrated functionality.
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: The functional mutations and behavioral test writes had clear task or restart-verification purposes, and the final node had no failed services, new listening exposure, or package-health damage. The only unnecessary retained mutation was staging residue created by cmd-eb295d88c6104ceb: /tmp/consumer.py.pre-repair, /tmp/consumer.py.repaired, and its generated /tmp/__pycache__ remained after completion instead of being cleaned up. This was low-risk but unreverted residue.
